name: Aeschines
summary:
Aeschines was a prominent Greek statesman and orator who played a significant role in the development of Athenian democracy.

As a member of the prominent Athenian family known as the Aeschines, he rose to prominence through his exceptional eloquence and mastery of rhetoric. By 350 BCE, he had become one of the ten most influential Attic orators, rivaled only by figures such as Demosthenes.

Aeschines' most notable achievement was his service as a prosecutor in several high-profile cases against rival politicians, including the infamous trial of Timocles.

His involvement with Timocles led to Aeschines' own downfall when he was eventually convicted and exiled. Despite this, his legacy continued to influence Athenian politics for generations.

Aeschines' impact on world history can be seen in the enduring power of Athenian democracy and the development of Western legal precedents.
